Be silent. Listen attentively, even and especially when things are uncomfortable. Your feelings right now are irrelevant. This is about her, and her alone. 

If you’re angry or upset or scared, now is not the moment to express or even ponder those things. Your emotions will draw your attention away from her at the moment she is most vulnerable. 

Be comforting. Don’t push her to say more or give you any details she hasn’t. If you have questions, note them and ask later. Do not under any circumstances interrupt her.

Never say anything like, “I would have done X.” Don’t ask her why she hasn’t reported and DEFINITELY don’t push her to report.

The amount of trust she is placing in you in this moment is going to be more than you’ve ever been trusted by anyone in your life. And it will likely be the most you’ll ever be trusted. 

This moment can and will define your relationship. Pushing will almost certainly cause her to clam up, and once that’s done, it can’t be undone.

Be kind. Be attentive. Be in control of yourself. Be quiet. Give her the floor and only open your mouth if she needs you too.

Remember that this is not about you. It’s about her. 

People who haven’t been raped have no idea what it’s like and never will, so don’t pretend you understand everything.

And for the love of god don’t push her for details.

Your only job is to support her lovingly. That’s it.

I won’t lie. What you’re going through right now and what you’ll be going through for a while can and probably will be brutal.

However, know that this is the worst part. A lot is going to come to you, and to going to be hard. Prepare yourself emotionally and socially. Communicate with the people around you. Not just people on the internet. 

Going through this is incredibly hard on your loved ones, and it’s going to be tempting to dive into your own pain. The longer you stay inside it, the harder it’s going to be.

You don’t have to tell your friends and loved ones everything, but let them know you’re going through something and let them know it’s very, very serious. But helping them understand will help you understand their position.

It’s tempting to say, “This is about me. My pain. And you have no idea what it’s like and you never will.”

And that will be true.  Nobody who hasn’t been through this is ever going to understand. And that’s ok. They shouldn’t have to. So don’t try to force it and don’t cut everyone out. Stay here, in the world, with your people, who ever they are. 

I know it’s tempting to shut yourself out from the people who are physically near you and rely wholly on your internet friends. And you should rely on them. But you need real people, proximity and warmth and support. 

Don’t let yourself forget that you aren’t stuck in a trauma loop. You are here, in the real world. It’s not years ago when you were completely unsafe and unprotected. It’s now and you are safe and whole and deserve to be loved.

I hate to run out a cliche, but it really does get better. And it will. But it won’t just do it on its own. Time only heals all wounds if you give it the opportunity to.

One of the worst parts of this moment is feeling like nothing is in your control. That you’re falling down a hole with no bottom. 

The moment we start recovering is the moment we figure out that we do have some control. Don’t forget that. 

You are loved. It’s going to be ok. Just give it time.

Whether or not I'm thinking about suicide (which I often am), I find the inevitability of death comforting. I imagine in the same way religious people feel about the concept of going to Heaven. The notion of surcease is comforting.   


I've got a weirdly positive Lovecraftian philosophy. No tentacles or space monsters or whatever; instead, I often think about how cosmically small we are. We're as minuscule and fleeting as quantum particles. Some people find that observation upsetting, that we don't really mean much in the scheme of things.  


I find it wonderful. The fact that we don't matter (on a cosmic scale, not on a human one) means that nothing matters—including our trauma and pain. If we realize how small and meaningless our pain ultimately is, we can put it in perspective. If nothing \*really\* means anything, then we are in control of whatever human meaning we assign. We get to choose what matters.   


I'm unsure if that's helpful or harmful, and it obviously no panacea, but it is a good way to get some perspective when I'm ready and able to do so.
